children: shares had erased earlier gains on Monday and fell nearly 1% even as Goldman Sachs upgraded the neocloud company and said the contract economics are likely to be stronger than investors expect.

“Going back to Finance 101, we see CoreWeave's enterprise value as being directly correlated to the magnitude and durability of the spread between its unlevered IRR and WACC—and we think investors may be underestimating the magnitude of upward revisions to uIRR, and overestimating the magnitude of upward revisions to WACC,” Goldman Sachs analyst Gabriela Borges wrote in a note to clients. Borges raised her rating to Buy from Neutral but lowered her price target to $106 from $129.

Delving deeper, Borges said she believes CoreWeave's annual recurring revenue per megawatt and unlevered IRR are “biased to the upside in the next 24 months because of tight supply, as well as our view that CoreWeave is differentiated from other neoclouds in its performance/cost metrics and its ability to execute on ramping new supply.”

The analyst also said that the company's blended cost of debt could move between 100 and 200 basis points higher, but not much more than that, ultimately putting a cap on its weighted cost of capital.
Shares of other neocloud companies, such as Nebius
, moved lower on the back of the upgrade.

title: CoreWeave gives up gains even as Goldman Sachs upgrades
